intro: A repeated token reads the same parameters at several positions. Its backward pass must collect contributions from every occurrence.
task: Scatter token-position gradients into a zero-initialized embedding-table gradient, adding repeated indices.
requirements: vocab_size is a positive integer excluding booleans. token_ids is a nonempty vector of integer values in vocabulary range.
upstream is a finite matrix with one row per token and at least one feature.
Return a NumPy array of shape (vocab_size, features). Unused token rows are zero; repeated rows sum rather than overwrite.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Allocate zeros with vocabulary rows, then add each position’s upstream vector.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: np.add.at handles repeated indices; advanced-indexed += may not accumulate them as intended.

explanation: Lookup copies a shared parameter row into each token position. By the chain rule, all paths from that shared parameter to the loss contribute to its gradient.
Scatter-add reverses gather: each upstream row adds into its token’s row. Ordinary assignment loses earlier contributions for repeated tokens.
Give two occurrences equal and opposite gradients. Predict the shared row’s update, then explain why counting occurrences alone cannot determine a gradient.
